Maintaining the 4.25–4.5% target range while continuing quantitative tightening and using “balanced risks” language points to a neutral-to-slightly hawkish stance: growth is solid and unemployment low, but “somewhat elevated” inflation keeps policy restrictive. This posture is consistent with flexible inflation-targeting and Taylor-rule frameworks that emphasize interest-rate smoothing and forward-looking, data-dependent adjustments (Clarida–Galí–Gertler; Taylor), and with inflation-at-risk research indicating residual upside inflation tails warrant caution. The balance sheet runoff and administered-rate settings (IORB/ON RRP) also imply continued liquidity withdrawal that can raise term premia (Cochrane–Piazzesi), moderating risk sentiment despite respectable real activity. Overall tone: modestly positive on growth, guarded on inflation.
